# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_010_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 2

**1** The tower was rising on a vast square rock — a rock older than the world itself. That rock was the tower's foundation. **2** Both the rock and its gate had been freshly cut. Six strong young men, all looking identical, were doing the building. **3** Thousands and thousands of other workers were hauling stones to the site — some from the sea, some from dry land. **4** Sea-stones were polished and perfectly square. Land-stones came in all kinds: square, round, smooth, rough. Some of the rough ones fit into the wall; others didn't fit at all. **5** The six young men were overseeing everything. I stood back and watched the tower go up. **6** It was going up beautifully and solidly. And around the tower stood seven women. The first was Faith; the second, Self-Restraint; the third, Power; the fourth, Patience; the fifth, Simplicity; the sixth, Innocence; the seventh, Purity. **7** The first woman was the strongest of them all — she was girded and ready for action. The others held hands and danced in a ring around the tower, joyfully.

---

*PNEUMA note: The dancing women around the tower is a striking image — virtue as dance, as the joyful order that surrounds God's building project. The image may reflect early Christian worship practice.*
